evidence.notes: The Martyrdom of Polycarp (c. 155-160 CE) was composed by the church of Smyrna as a circular letter. Polycarp is its subject; the Smyrnaean community authored it.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: We learned the plan of salvation from those through whom the Gospel came to us. Matthew issued a written Gospel among the Hebrews while Peter and Paul were preaching at Rome. Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down what Peter had preached. Luke, Paul's companion, recorded his Gospel. Afterwards John, who leaned on the Lord's breast, published his Gospel during his residence at Ephesus.

subject_entity.notes: Founder of Montanism (the 'New Prophecy') in Phrygia c. 155–180. Claimed to speak as the Paraclete in the first person. Associated with prophetesses Maximilla and Priscilla (Prisca). Montanism taught rigorous fasting, the imminent New Jerusalem descending at Pepuza, and the continuation of ecstatic prophecy — generating controversy with emerging episcopal authority.

object_entity.proposition_label: Prophetic Gifts Continue After the Apostles
object_entity.description: The Holy Spirit continues to give direct prophecy and ecstatic spiritual gifts beyond the apostolic age; new prophetic revelation may supplement or correct the established tradition. Affirmed by Montanists; opposed by the emerging episcopal mainstream who grounded authority in apostolic succession.

evidence.notes: Montanus claimed to speak as the Paraclete — direct affirmation of continuing ecstatic prophecy.

passage.excerpt: At this time in Phrygia, Montanus, as he was called, together with Alcibiades and Theodotus, gave the adversary occasion to suppose that he was the Paraclete. He was seized with frenzy and began to babble and utter strange sounds, prophesying contrary to the established custom of the Church handed down from the beginning. Of those who listened to this spurious utterance, some were vexed and rebuked him as one that was possessed and controlled by a demon — but others were elated, thinking this was the gift of the Spirit.
